holidays.name: National Moldy Cheese Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate cheeses that are meant to be moldy, not the forgotten block at the back of your fridge. Blue cheeses like Gorgonzola and Stilton bring sharp, tangy bite. Bloomy-rind cheeses like Brie and Camembert are milder and creamier. Build a cheese board and let the good mold win.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. No founder or organization has claimed it, and the earliest known print mention dates to 2001.
holidays.funFact: Cheesemakers control temperature, humidity and timing so that only the intended mold grows. The molds used in cheesemaking are safe to eat.

holidays.name: Curious Events Day
holidays.description: A salute to the strange, the unexplained and the wonderfully weird. Swap a boring afternoon for a trip to a local haunted spot, a roadside oddity or a spooky legend. Swap odd-but-true stories with friends while you're at it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits neatly into the spooky run-up to Halloween.
holidays.funFact: It lands in the middle of October, when interest in ghost stories, haunted sites and unexplained mysteries is at its peak.

holidays.name: International Beer and Pizza Day
holidays.description: Two of the world's most beloved comfort foods get a day together. Pair a crisp lager with a classic margherita, or a hoppy IPA with a loaded pepperoni pie, and call it a celebration.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, and the pairing needs little explanation.
holidays.funFact: Both beer and pizza are built on fermentation. Yeast makes the beer bubbly and the pizza dough rise.
